newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria says no peace until Israel changes practices.
newsitem.headline: Syria says no peace until Israel changes practices.

text.p: Syrian newspapers on Tuesday accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government of creating a war-like atmosphere, saying there would be no peace until he left power or Israel changed its practices.
The official newspapers condemned Israel's commando attack on Hizbollah guerrillas in south Lebanon on Monday and punitive measures against Palestinians.
They urged the United States to act quickly to save the peace process and called on Arabs to cut all ties with the Jewish state.
"The Netanyahu government works to escalate tension, create atmospheres of war and push the region to an endless chasm," al-Thawra daily said.

"That means peace is still a far-fetched dream and the process is still deadlocked until the time comes when Netanyahu's government has either changed its extremist and provocative practices, or Netanyahu quits rule in Israel."

"The terrorist operation in south Lebanon...is a new episode of the provocative, sabotaging and destructive policy of the hardline and racist government of Netanyahu which is aimed at ending the peace process completely," the ruling party newspaper al-Baath said.
Sporadic Syrian-Israeli peace talks were further deadlocked when the Likud leader rejected withdrawal from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967, in return for peace with Syria.
Syria wants full withdrawal from the strategic plateau. Israel's former Labour government said withdrawal would match the depth of peace ties between the two countries.
"It is a terrorist country that speaks no language but war and aggression and thinks only of expansion and settlements," al-Thawra said.

"The U.S. is demanded, now and more than anytime in the past, to move quickly to curb the aggressive outbursts of Netanyahu and take proper action to defuse tension and stop this government from continuing its destructive policy."
Al-Baath called for "deterrent measures" against Israel and urged Arabs to "cut all diplomatic and economic ties with the Zionist entity and halt all forms of normalisation".
"If the world wants peace, then it should impose sanctions on Israel to force it to go back to sense and logic...and thus save peace from its crisis," it added.
